Rule: Break the enemy Base before yours falls. Each Base has 5 orbs.
Each side plays a 12-card deck. A Cowboy deck needs at least one Sheriff and must respect each card's copy limit.
Each side draws 4 cards. A seed decides the shuffle and who acts first in round 1. The first seat alternates every round.
Each side has three lanes. A lane holds one troop.
Summon up to one troop and cast up to one spell. Both are optional. If you want both, summon first.
Troops with 1 to 4 stars are free. 5 or 6 stars cost one of your troops. 7 or more cost two. The new troop may take a lane a tribute left.
A spell removes one orb from an enemy troop. Lasso and Singularity may also move a surviving troop one lane into an empty lane.
A troop whose card says Ride may move one lane into an empty lane of yours instead of summoning. It keeps its orbs, and a spell may follow.
After both sides act, every troop strikes the troop across from it at the same time. A troop brought to zero orbs still lands its hit.
A troop with no enemy across from it hits the enemy Base for its attack.
A blocker absorbs the whole hit, however few orbs it has. Nothing spills over to the Base.
Each side draws one card at the start of every round after the first. An empty deck draws nothing.
The duel ends when a Base reaches zero. If both fall in the same clash it is a draw. After round 9 the side with more Base orbs wins, and equal orbs is a draw.
In a Wanted hunt the boss side holds its lanes and only strikes at the clash, and every one of your troops may Ride. Defeat the boss while your Base stands.
Clearing all five hunts of a boss earns its card. Six Frontier cards unlock at 2 to 7 counted duel wins. Practice and hunts do not count as wins.
Only in the Dragon Fire arc: a Dragon's damage beyond its blocker's last orb hits that side's Base.
